Items.Authors: Jason E. Austermann, James Beall, Andrew Forsman, Haibo Huang, Johannes Hubmayr, Matthew Koc, Jeffrey van Lanen, Pavel Lapa, Joshua Raimist, Jordan Stutz, Anatolios Tambazidis, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Laser-micromachined silicon platelet feedhorns for large-scale, submillimeter and millimeter-wave focal planes
Items.Abstract: We present the fabrication and characterization of the world’s first 150~mm diameter silicon platelet feedhorn array produced using laser micromachining. This feedhorn array is designed to operate in the submillimeter band centered at 350 GHz (330--370 GHz). We compare the performance of this array directly to those produced using traditional deep reactive-ion etching (DRIE), as well as to simulation. We present optical performance measurements at room-temperature and cryogenically coupled to KID detectors. In addition, we review and compare these results to a demonstration of laser-micromachined feedhorns designed for the millimeter-wave band of 80–160 GHz (i.e. typical CMB bands). Finally, we also present an exploration into additional advantages of laser-micromachining, including sidewall control and the potential of using thicker (and thus fewer) wafers, which could significantly reduce production costs and labor.

Items.Authors: Matteo Lombini, Michele Bellazzini, Emiliano Diolaiti, Fernando Pedichini, Andrea Baruffolo, Federico Battaini, Enrico Cascone, Fausto Cortecchia, Felice Cusano, Andrea Di Paola, Christian Eredia, Jacopo Farinato, Andrea Grazian, Diego Paris, Salvatore Savarese, Pietro Schipani, Laura Schreiber, Enzo Brocato, Roberto Gilli, Marco Mignoli, Fabio Vito, David E. Trilling, Dennis Zaritsky
Items.Title: LBCmos: extending wide-field imaging and photometry capabilities at LBTO to the next decades
Items.Abstract: LBCmos upgrades the Large Binocular Camera with new 8k × 8k sCMOS detectors, providing improved efficiency, fast readout, full-field coverage, and new narrow and medium-band filters. The redesign maintains the optical performance of LBC while modernizing mechanics, electronics, and software. Enhanced operational flexibility enables fast photometry and real-time diagnostics. LBCmos strengthens LBTO’s competitiveness in wide-field imaging and expands its scientific capabilities from stellar populations to high-redshift surveys.

Items.Authors: Nathan P. Magari, James E. Larkin, Shelley A. Wright, Bryson Cale, Michael P. Fitzgerald
Items.Title: Liger at W.M. Keck Observatory: lenslet IFS spectral extraction techniques
Items.Abstract: Liger is a next-generation imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) currently being fabricated for the Keck I telescope. Liger will be delivered with a data reduction system (DRS) to produce science-quality images and IFS data cubes. In this paper we investigate advanced spectral extraction techniques for Liger’s lenslet mode. Using end-to-end simulations of the instrument optics and detector response, we optimize the spectral extraction algorithm based on accuracy, computational efficiency, and memory usage. In particular we explore a full 2-D convolution of the raw frame using a spectral point spread function (PSF) characterized by simulated arc lamp scans. We find that this procedure provides improved SNR in the reduced data cube compared to previous methods.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Wenner, Joseph H. Silber, Andrew Hope, Michael Schubnell, David Schlegel, William V. Shourt, Robert Besuner
Items.Title: Linear motion flexure (“R-FLEX”) for miniature 6.2 mm pitch optical fiber positioning robots with polar (R-θ) kinematics
Items.Abstract: R-FLEX is a compact flexure-based radial positioning mechanism for next-generation fiber-fed spectroscopic telescope instruments. Designed to fit within a ø5.8 mm package at 6.2 mm pitch—2.5-3x denser than current systems—it delivers ≤5 μm RMS positioning accuracy over a 4 mm travel range. Development utilized parametric optimization, finite element analysis, and fabrication and testing of prototypes. Measured performance met or exceeded requirements across all key metrics. R-FLEX is a promising candidate for mass deployment of precision robotic fiber positioners for future cosmological surveys, supporting the collection of hundreds of millions of galaxy spectra to study the large-scale structure of the universe.

Items.Authors: Lawrence M. Machia, Alan Vasquez Soto, Nicholas M. Law, Glenn Walters, Amy S. Ishiguro, Mike Ronco, Collin H. Grimes, Thomas Procter, Megan M. Dubay, Hank Corbett, Alex Bucheli, Jonathan Carney, Thomas Cowart, James A. Dockery, Katie M. Fasbender, Shannon K. Fitton, William J. Marshall, Donovan G. Schlekat
Items.Title: Lining it up: integrated focus and tilt alignment system for the Argus Array
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array is an 8-meter class, all-sky optical survey designed to discover transient events via sub-minute deep imaging. The instrument is comprised of 1200 individual telescopes and cameras which together observe the entire accessible sky simultaneously. The scale of the array presents an operational challenge for focusing and tilt-alignment in reasonable construction timescales. While off-the-shelf robotic focusers are relatively common, most instruments are manually tilt-aligned with shims. The number of telescopes in the Argus array precludes manual tilt-alignment. Here we present design and prototype of a custom Argus robotic alignment system which integrates focus and tilt-alignment capability into a single low-cost device.

Items.Authors: Anastasios Aretos, Younes Chahid, Chris Miller, Mark Cliffe, Graham Wilks, Lee Chapman, Scott McPhee
Items.Title: Liquid nitrogen pre-cooling system for ELT instruments utilising additively manufactured heat exchangers, integrated temperature and liquid level control
Items.Abstract: We propose an advanced alternative pre-cooling system architecture which uses additively manufactured heat exchangers with increased surface areas, embedded liquid level sensors as well as integrated heating elements, that provide tighter control over the pre-cooling process. We provide a comparison between the effects that the build material selection has to the manufacturing methods employed as well as the internal geometry of the heat exchanger. By using the incumbent pre-cooling system of HARMONI, as a base line we offer a comparison on the improvements that such a system offers over current and near future designs, both in cooling performance as well as system integration and overall manufacturing costs.

Items.Authors: Jakub Ripa, Filip Münz, Marianna Dafčíková, András Pál, Norbert Werner, Masanori Ohno, László Mészáros, Balázs Csák, Pavel Kosík, Michaela Ďuríšková, Lea Szakszonová, Martin Kolář, Tomáš Vítek, Nikola Husáriková, Filip Hroch, Michal Pazderka, Yasushi Fukazawa, Hiromitsu Takahashi, Tsunefumi Mizuno, Jean-Paul Breuer, Masato Yokota, Kazuhiro Nakazawa, Hirokazu Odaka, Yuto Ichinohe, Tomáš Urbanec, Aleš Povalač, Miroslav Kasal, Miroslav Šmelko, Peter Hanák, Gábor Galgóczi, Martin Topinka, Hsiang-Kuang Chang, Tsung-Che Liu, Chih-Hsun Lin, Chin-Ping Hu, Che-Chih Tsao, Kaustubha Sen, Chih-En Wu, Jakub Kapuš, Ján Hudec, Marcel Frajt, Maksim Rezenov, Vladimír Dániel, Petr Svoboda, Juraj Dudáš, Martin Sabol, Ivo Veřtát, Róbert László, Martin Koleda
Items.Title: Long-term performance of SiPMs in space environment measured by GRBAlpha, GRBBeta, and VZLUSAT-2 CubeSats
Items.Abstract: We report the successful application of silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) in gamma-ray burst detectors used in GRBAlpha, GRBBeta, and VZLUSAT-2 CubeSats operating in the low Earth orbit (LEO) radiation environment. We describe the changes in the dark count rate and low-energy threshold of S13360-3050 PE MPPCs by Hamamatsu, based on measurements spanning over four years. We have demonstrated that SiPMs, shielded by 2.5 mm of PbSb alloy, can be used in a LEO environment on a scientific mission lasting beyond four years. This shows the potential for SiPMs to be employed in future satellites.

Items.Authors: Matthew A. Koc, Jason E. Austermann, James A. Beall, Johannes Hubmayr, Joel N. Ullom, Michael R. Vissers, Jordan D. Wheeler
Items.Title: Low-temperature performance of silicon micromachined waveguide filter-banks
Items.Abstract: Line Intensity Mapping has great promise to allow us deeper insight and provide better constraints into a variety of cosmological studies. To enable this technology, we need compact and high efficiency spectrometers that are scalable. One such spectrometer is the waveguide filter-bank. Here we present the design, fabrication, and optical testing of a silicon micromachined prototype at room and cryogenic temperatures. This device is designed in a split-block architecture and can be readily fabricated using silicon micromachining processes. Compared to the lossless design which has a maximum spectral efficiency of 0.5, the single-channel (260 GHz), gold-plated prototype was measured to have a maximum spectral efficiency over 0.29 with a resolving power of R = 263 when measured at room temperature. We measure that the Qloss of the filter increases from approximately 1100 at room temperature to approximately 3000 at cryogenic temperatures.

Items.Authors: Runa Briguglio, Matteo Menessini, Marco Xompero, Ciro Del Vecchio, Daniele Gallieni, Matteo Tintori
Items.Title: Mass budget analysis for a contactless active mirror for space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Active mirrors are considered key components for future large aperture space telescopes such as the HWO. Recently, a technology based on contactless active mirrors, developed for ground based observatory, has been proposed and preliminary tested in the lab. In a contactless active mirror, the optical surface is a thin Zerodur glass shell controlled by voice coil actuators and monitored by capacitive sensors; as a result, the optical surface is mechanically decoupled from the support. Such point has relevant implications from a system-wise perspective, as the support structure has no optical specifications any longer: in particular, the support may be extremely light-weighted, while having little to no print-through on the optical surface. The concept has been preliminary demonstrated on a 40 cm diameter prototype with 19 actuators, featuring an areal density as low as 18 kg/m2. In this work we discuss the as-build mass budget and present a roadmap to further improve the mass budget.

Items.Authors: Anthony Soulain, Alexis Matter, Philippe Bério, Stéphane Lagarde, Romain Petrov, Florentin Millour, Bruno Lopez
Items.Title: MATISSE-py: a high-level python interface for efficient, automated VLTI/MATISSE data reduction
Items.Abstract: We present MATISSE-py, a Python package automating the complex reduction of VLTI/MATISSE interferometric data. It provides a modular abstraction layer over the official ESO pipeline, enabling scripted workflows, batch processing, and integration with modern data-analysis environments. We also introduce enhanced calibration algorithms - including refined BCD correction, robust transfer function handling, and v-factor computation - derived from seven years of operations, significantly improving data quality. Featuring robust quality control, interactive Plotly visualizations, and full compatibility with official binaries, MATISSE-py streamlines reduction for both experts and new users, paving the way for a modernized, reproducible reduction ecosystem.

Items.Authors: Elia Costa, Bernardo Salasnich, Andrea Baruffolo, Mirko Colapietro, Fabio Rossi, Salvatore Savarese
Items.Title: MAVIS instrument control software system: post-FDR update and redesign of the interface with the two PFDMs
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (Multi-conjugate Adaptive optics Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a next-generation adaptive optics instrument designed for the VLT AOF, and its Instrument Control Software System (ICSS) plays a key role in its operation. This paper presents the current design of the MAVIS ICSS following a successful Final Design Review (FDR) in October 2025. The ICSS has undergone a critical update that includes the complete redesign of the interface with the two Post-Focal Deformable Mirrors (PFDMs). This new interface has been seamlessly integrated within the ESO Instrument Software Framework (IFW). A key architectural change involves moving the complexity of the PFDM interaction to the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), where the actual control logic is implemented. Besides the monitoring, the ICSS allows for non-real-time control of the Deformable Mirrors (DM), a functionality highly useful during the Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) phase.

Items.Authors: Paolo Cerpelloni, Luca Marafatto, Davide Greggio, Matteo Aliverti, Stefan Ströbele, Mirko Colapietro, Simone Doniselli, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Maria Bergomi, Valentina Viotto, François Rigaut
Items.Title: MAVIS: AIV procedures for the post focal relay
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the alignment concept, workflow, and tooling developed for the MAVIS PFR (Post Focal  Relay) Assembly, Integration and Verification phase at the Astronomical Observatory of Padova. We describe  the reference architecture, measurement strategy, error budget, and sequencing logic that enable alignment of  the entire PFR chain to the required tolerances, highlighting the advantages and constraints of this hybrid  mechanical–optical approach.

Items.Authors: Paolo Cerpelloni, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Alessandro Ballone, Davide Greggio, Matteo Aliverti, Luca Marafatto, Mirko Colapietro, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Daniele Vassallo, Gabriele Umbriaco, Elena Carolo, Bernardo Salasnich, Elia Costa, Daniela Fantinel, Andrea Baruffolo, Maria Bergomi, Valentina Viotto, François Rigaut
Items.Title: MAVIS: diagnostic and NCPA unit and its laboratory verification
Items.Abstract: MAVIS Diagnostic and NCPA Unit (DNU) consists of two identical CMOS cameras mounted on a common linear stage. While the first camera allows for the on-axis pupil imaging mode, the second one, equipped with a multi-lenslet array, enables for the on-axis wavefront sensing mode. Although not planned to be used during night operations, the DNU wavefront sensing mode may be useful during the initial nighttime commissioning to measure on-axis residual aberrations and wavefront error in the entire light path with and without Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics loop running. In this proceeding, we describe the MAVIS DNU component, its functionalities, and its laboratory verification.

Items.Authors: Anthony J. Horton, Andrea Bianco, David Brodrick, Jennifer Burgess, David Clarke, Timothy Chin, Elia Costa, Mark Downing, Simon Ellis, Nuwanthika Fernando, Michele Frangiamore, Gaston Gausachs, Miguel Gonzalez Bolivar, Davide Greggio, Max Hewlett, Johan Kosmalski, Summer Luo, Nuria Lorente, Richard McDermid, Helen McGregor, Trevor Mendel, Brent Miszalski, Jonathan Moller, Tristan Monnier, Francois Rigaut, David Robertson, Bernardo Salasnich, Warrick Schofield, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Scott Smedley, Annino Vaccarella, Lew Waller, Ross Zhelem, Jessica Zheng
Items.Title: MAVIS: science instruments final design
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Adaptive Optics Module, working together with the Adaptive Optics Facility of VLT Unit Telescope 4, will deliver a diffraction limited field 30 arcseconds in diameter at visible wavelengths. This will enable an unprecedented combination of spatial resolution, sensitivity and field of view, opening up new regions of parameter space for scientific exploration. To capitalise on this capability MAVIS needs two scientific instruments; a multi-band imager covering the full 30 arcsecond corrected field while sampling the diffraction limited PSF, and an integral field spectrograph covering the full range of visible wavelengths. In this paper we describe the design of the MAVIS Imager and Spectrograph as presented at the recent MAVIS Final Design Review, and discuss some of the challenges, trade offs, and processes which led us to these designs.

Items.Authors: Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Prashant Pathak, Abhirami S. Raghu, Benjamin Courtney-Barrer, Roy van Boekel, Thomas Bertram, Markus Feldt, Matthew A. Kenworthy, Bernhard Brandl
Items.Title: Maximising the mid-infrared high-contrast performance on ELT/METIS despite water vapour seeing
Items.Abstract: The Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) will be equipped with a SCAO system delivering Strehl ratios around 99% in the N band (8-13µm). Yet, the actual wavefront quality seen by the METIS coronagraphic modules will be significantly affected by water vapour seeing. We analyse two years of VLTI/GRAVITY fringe tracker archives to assess the variability of differential water vapour column density at milli-second timescales on ELT scales. Our analysis suggests that water vapour seeing will add a median wavefront error of about 175 nm RMS at N band. If not corrected, this effect will degrade the achievable sensitivity limits in terms of contrast by more than 2 magnitudes. To mitigate this effect, we plan to deploy a focal-plane wavefront sensing and control algorithm based on an asymmetric pupil concept using a deep learning approach. We describe the expected performance of this secondary wavefront control loop, and its consequences on the METIS high-contrast performance.

Items.Authors: Lukas Rimmele, André Fehlmann, Isabelle Scholl
Items.Title: Mechanical design of resolver positioned cryogenic filter wheels
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic Near Infrared Spectropolarimeter (Cryo-NIRSP) at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) operates four filter and slit wheels on optical benches stabilized at 60 Kelvin. Because the slits lie at the focal plane, they must be positioned with high precision and repeatability. The instrument therefore relies on accurate wheel position feedback to select among various slit and filter configurations. The previous design used limit switches to verify wheel positions, but thermal cycling and mechanical runout led to unreliable feedback. A new wheel assembly has been developed that incorporates a magnetic resolver directly coupled to each wheel, providing accurate and robust rotational feedback suitable for cryogenic operation. This paper outlines the mechanical considerations and design approaches used to integrate the resolver into a cryogenic environment to improve positioning accuracy, reliability, and overall instrument performance.

Items.Authors: S. Rabien, L. Busoni, C. Del Vecchio, J. Ziegleder, R. S. Miller, R. Saathof, U. Wittrock, T. Ott, M. Erhard, P. Buschkamp, A. Riccardi, M. Bonaglia
Items.Title: Membrane space telescope: packaging and deployment
Items.Abstract: Membrane mirror technology offers the prospect for future extremely large space telescopes. Utilizing a thin parabolic membrane as primary mirror base, very low aerial weights can be achieved. The flexible nature of those mirrors allows to roll those up for launch un unwrap in orbit. In this paper we will show a proposed foldable structure that can be compactly stored with the mirror in a launch fairing and deployed in space. With a scaled prototype model, we illustrate the system’s compact stowage and deployment character.

Items.Authors: Mohammad N. Islam, Aditya Krishna Karigiri Madhusudhan, James Trudel, Jagdish Singh, Tayron Dueck, Gordon Lacy, Richard Hellyer, Brian Hoff
Items.Title: Metrology-based surface and alignment verification of the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-transient Detector antennas
Items.Abstract: The Canadian Hydrogen Observatory for Radio-transient Detector (CHORD) is a next-generation radio array of 512 six‑meter composite antennas being built at the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory in British Columbia. The shape of composite reflectors are dependent on many factors such as mold accuracy, process induced errors, temperature, fabrication technique, post-production operations, etc. Surface distortion and alignment errors require higher degree of repeatability to meet various science goals. This paper presents metrology and manufacturing results from over 50 antennas using laser tracker and photogrammetry data. Surface errors average 0.5 mm RMS and alignment accuracy is within 1 arcminute, confirming that the composite fabrication process meets CHORD’s demanding performance and scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Silvio Di Rosa, Demetrio Magrin, Davide Greggio, Mohamed Yahia Bournane, Stefano Ciroi, Giovanni Boato, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Roberto Ragazzoni, Mario Salatti, Matteo Aliverti, Andrea Baruffolo, Luigi Lessio, Marco Dima, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Paolo Cerpelloni, Simonetta Chinellato, Simone Di Filippo, Jacopo Farinato, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Luca Marafatto, Matteo Munari, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Marco Riva, Enrico Cappellaro, Valentina Viotto, Simone Zaggia
Items.Title: MezzoCielo: from the 40cm prototype toward a 1m class monocentric all-sky telescope
Items.Abstract: MezzoCielo (Italian word for “Half of the Sky”) aims to be a revolutionary optical system, combining a relatively large aperture with an extremely wide Field of View. The telescope is based upon the concept of a central monocentric lens, comprehending a dodecahedral frame filled with low refractive index-high transparency optical fluid. The seeing-limited performances are reached through the use of a large number of identical cameras, located on the focal surface of the central sphere.   In this work, we will describe the current status of the instrument, focusing upon the mechanical investigation of the monocentric structure, the optical design of the correcting cameras and the path towards the construction of a small-scale prototype. Possible strategies for handling the huge quantity of data coming from the single observation will be investigated as well.

Items.Authors: Andrea Tozzi, Lorenzo Pino, Leonardo Testi, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Erika Calaon, Paolo Giacobbe, Fabio D'Anca, Riccado Lilli, Javier Pèrez Alvarez, Paolo Picchi, Antonio Scippa, Ernesto Oliva
Items.Title: MICHELANGELO: a compact, high-resolution mid-infrared spectrograph with a space-qualifiable germanium immersion grating
Items.Abstract: MICHELANGELO is a proposed high-dispersion infrared spectrograph for exoplanetary atmosphere characterization in the 3-5 μm range, providing high-resolution spectroscopy (R > 50,000) in the L and M bands. This wavelength region is rich in diagnostic molecular features from sulfur-, nitrogen- species, optimal for detecting cooler exoplanets. We present the conceptual design employing innovative germanium immersion grating technology to achieve simultaneous L-band (2.9-4.2 μm) and M-band (4.3-5.5 μm) coverage in a compact design. The configuration uses two independent cross-dispersed echelle spectrographs (70×40×40 cm per unit), enablingh sensitivity for direct imaging of spatially resolved young planets and emission spectroscopy of transiting exoplanets. The compact design suits 8-10m class telescopes with adaptive optics and future space missions. MICHELANGELO bridges current facilities and future ELT instrumentation, offering 4-8 times detection speed improvement.

Items.Authors: Miranda Eiben, Jón Guðmundsson, Rustam Balafendiev, Thomas Gascard
Items.Title: Millimeter and sub-millimeter characterization of polymers used for infrared filters in high-sensitivity cryogenic microwave telescopes
Items.Abstract: Infrared filters are an important transmissive optical component in millimeter receivers, as they reduce radiative loading on cold stages, thereby improving cryogenic performance. However, the complex optical properties of the materials commonly used for these filters are poorly characterized, particularly in-band and in the sub-millimeter regime. The absorption and scattering properties of these materials are becoming increasingly important for designing high-sensitivity millimeter instruments, as their loosely constrained properties are one of the greatest sources of uncertainty remaining in white noise modeling. We report the absorption in the millimeter and sub-millimeter regime of nylon 6, nylon 6/6, PTFE and polyethylene (both bulk HDPE and foam HDPE used in radio transparent filter stacks). Additionally, we report the relative power scattered out of the main beam by these materials from 90 to 330 GHz, measured in free space by a robot-enabled scanning vector network analyzer.

Items.Authors: Oleksandra Rebrysh, Lorenzo Merli, Alessandro Ballone, Valentina Viotto, Davide Greggio, Simone Di Filippo, Luca Marafatto, David Barr, Sylvain Cetre, Federico Battaini, Gabriele Umbriaco, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Elena Carolo, Tânia Machado, Edoardo Bellone de Grecis, Silvio Di Rosa
Items.Title: MiniMATTO: towards the practical implementation of the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: MiniMATTO is a predecessor of the MATTO (Multi-conjugate Adaptive Techniques Test Optics) bench,  being developed at INAF-OAPd. Given the complexity of the final system, dedicated validation of hardware  components, control strategies, and software pipelines are required prior to full-scale implementation.  In this work, we present the optomechanical design of miniMATTO, a simplified platform developed to  support the integration and verification of key MCAO technologies. The bench incorporates three natural guide  star sources, two DMs, and three SLM-based wavefront  sensing channels operating in focal plane configurations.  We also report the results of the first experimental campaigns performed on miniMATTO. These include  synchronization tests across the turbulence injection, wavefront sensing, and correction stages, evaluation of  wavefront sensing accuracy using SLM-generated WFS configurations, and preliminary closed-loop control experiments employing the DAO4MATTO framework.

Items.Authors: Eleonora Barbavara, Giovanni Isopi, Alessandro Attoli, Elia Stefano Battistelli, Paolo de Bernardis, Federico Cacciotti, Giuseppe Carboni, Ettore Carretti, Daniele Ciccalotti, Fabio Columbro, Alessandro Coppolecchia, Angelo Cruciani, Giuseppe D'Alessandro, Marco De Petris, Federica Govoni, Adelaide Ladu, Luca Lamagna, Pasqualino Marongiu, Silvia Masi, Matteo Murgia, Alessandro Navarrini, Alessandro Novelli, Andrea Occhiuzzi, Andrea Orlati, Alessandro Paiella, Giorgio Pettinari, Francesco Piacentini, Mauro Pili, Tonino Pisanu, Sergio Poppi, Luca Schirru, Gian Paolo Vargiu, Sofia Ferazzoli, Costanza Bellucci, Davide Marsala, Chiara Volpe, Giancarlo De Gasperis, Giampaolo Pisano
Items.Title: MISTRAL: optical alignment and beam optimization at the Sardinia Radio Telescope
Items.Abstract: The MIllimeter Sardinia radio Telescope Receiver based on Array of Lumped elements KIDs (MISTRAL) is a cryogenic W-band LEKID camera installed at the Gregorian focus of the 64-m fully steerable radio telescope Sardinia Radio Telescope (SRT), in Italy, in May 2023. MISTRAL will take advantage of its 12 arcseconds of angular resolution, a 4 arcminutes wide instantaneous field of view and its high sensitivity, to be one of the most competitive instrument to observe the mm-wave sky. In this contribution an overview of the technical commissioning will be given, detailing on the optical alignment of the SRT's mirror as well as the analysis done for the beam optization.

Items.Authors: Hanshin Lee, Casey Kyte, John Good, Brian L. Vattiat, Gary J. Hill, Joshua Oppor
Items.Title: Mix and match as you go: evaluation of the beam switch module with production integral field unit fiber cables for VIRUS2 instrument
Items.Abstract: Previously, we detailed the development of the Beam Switch Module (BSM) for the VIRUS2 instrument and its integration/alignment results. The BSM distills the beam switching functions that many traditional spectrographs accomplished inside the spectrograph themselves into an independent module outside the spectrographs, but at the same time adding a double beam scrambling and fiber switching functions, thereby making the instrument compact, modular, stable, and scalable. Inevitably, having a separate BSM means extra throughput loss due to additional components involved. Our BSM R&D effort so far has shown this “perceived” loss can in fact be minimal, and, in return, the instrument can potentially be adaptable to observing modes that would otherwise require new instruments. We constructed a production BSM (BSM3) with fully assembled VIRUS2 IFUs integrated/aligned to the BSM. We detail the integration and alignment process and compare its measured throughput against the expectations.

Items.Authors: Hiro Otsuka, Takanori Sakamoto, Yuta Kawakubo, Motoko Serino, Hsien-Chieh Shen, Ryota Kamimura, Shinpei Kubodera, Yuki Sato, Taiji Hayashi, Takumi Maeyama
Items.Title: Modeling of curvature deviations in micropore optics for 6U CubeSat mission SEAGULL
Items.Abstract: SEAGULL is a 6U CubeSat mission designed to search for electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave events. For its X-ray telescope, we plan to use micro-pore optics (MPOs) manufactured by Exosens Inc. Each MPO has a nominal curvature radius of 600 mm. By arranging four MPOs in a 2 × 2 configuration on a common spherical surface, the telescope can achieve a wide field of view of 8 deg × 8 deg. However, the actual curvature of MPOs varies depending on the manufacturing process, and the curvature difference should affect the X-ray focusing performance. To evaluate the focusing performance of MPOs more precisely, we analyzed the focal positions of locally irradiated X-rays on a single MPO and developed a simulator that incorporates curvature deviations introduced during manufacturing. We report the focusing characteristics obtained using this geometry-based simulator and discuss challenges in assembling X-ray telescopes using multiple MPOs.

Items.Authors: Paula Betancourt Esparza, Salvador Cuevas, Luis Martinez Vázquez, Leonardo Garcés García, Carolina Keiman, Luis Álvarez Nuñez, Beatriz Sánchez, Mamadou N'Diaye, Arthur Vigan
Items.Title: Molecular mapping with the FRIDA instrument using NVIDIA GPU-based parallel computing
Items.Abstract: FRIDA is a forthcoming near-infrared integral-field spectrograph for the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). We present a high-performance parallel computing pipeline in C++/CUDA utilizing NVIDIA GPUs to execute large-scale molecular mapping via high-resolution cross-correlation, an essential technique for exoplanet atmospheric characterization. The architecture processes spectral data cubes (60 x 64 x 1024) pixel by pixel, running three customized CUDA kernels in practically real time. Validated with synthetic observations containing controlled H2O targets, the pipeline successfully isolated all sources from noise, accurately distinguishing rest-frame baselines from line broadening, Doppler shifts, and coupled kinematic effects. The collapsed molecular map confirmed the pipeline's sensitivity to sub-resolution properties. This framework is fully engineered to process real science-grade data upon FRIDA's first light.

Items.Authors: Kevin Luke, Myriam Rodrigues, Mathieu Puech, Nicholas Boardman, Vivienne Wild, Oscar Gonzalez, Michele Cirasuolo
Items.Title: MOONS1D: one dimensional science simulator for VLT/MOONS
Items.Abstract: MOONS1D is a new one dimensional science simulator for Multi-Object Optical and Near-infrared Spectrograph (MOONS) at VLT. MOONS1D is a collection of python modules which enable simulation of spectra with astrophysical templates, instrument response of MOONS and atmospheric effects. Simulation is run by standard ESO configuration files and the output is modelled according to the data model of MOONS.

Items.Authors: Marco Bonaglia, Lorenzo Busoni, Guido Agapito, Giulia Carlà, Cédric Plantet, Tommaso Lapucci, Dheeraj Malik, Alfio Puglisi, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Marco Riva, Giorgio Pariani, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO at ELT: LOR WFS module final design overview
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   The Low-Order and Reference Wavefront Sensor (LOR WFS) Module is a critical subsystem, comprising three identical units to measure low-order aberrations from Natural Guide Stars (NGS) across an 80 arcsec technical field of view. The final design utilizes high-stiffness acquisition stages (AST) capable of 600 mm x 300 mm travel and incorporates an anti-collision system (ACS) to ensure safe operation. Each LOR WFS unit is equipped with a visible-band Reference (R) WFS and a J+H band Low-Order (LO) WFS, with the LO channel configurable as either a full-aperture sensor (including a LIFT option) or a 2x2 Shack-Hartmann sensor.   This paper gives an overview of the design and technical challenges of the subsystem at the time of the subsystem final design review.

Items.Authors: Benedetta Di Francesco, Gianluca Di Rico, Ivan Di Antonio, Angelo Valentini, Simone Benedetti, Fabio Di Nicola, Amico Di Cianno, Fiorella Nusca, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Elisa Portaluri, Mauro Dolci
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: test and verification steps towards the calibration unit final design
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. As in any complex system designed for ELT-class telescopes, MORFEO relies on the coordinated operations of its internal subsystems. Among these, the Calibration Unit (CU) is an opto-mechanical system which projects a set of sources on the telescope focal planes, allowing for calibrations and test procedures. After the Preliminary Design Review, the subsystem is now advancing through the Final Design Phase.  During the last period, the CU underwent extensive laboratory testing to verify compliance with key requirements and to validate its current design. In parallel with the test results, the electronic and software control architectures have been consolidated as well. This contribution summarizes the results of these activities towards a matured CU design.

Items.Authors: Wenli Xu, Walter Seifert, Gavin Dalton, Myriam Rodrigues, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Andreas Kelz, Ramon Navarro, Rick Romp
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: evolutions of the optical design for the VIS spectrograph
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is a Multi-Object Spectrograph for the 39-meter ESO ELT in Chile. The instrument allows for a multiplex of 140 in the visible and 180 in the near-infrared wavelength ranges. Its Integral Field Units offer parallel observation of eight extended objects. As an ELT second generation instrument its architecture has experienced several major evolutions in order to maximize the instrument efficiency and minimize the risk and budget.   The optical design of the VIS spectrograph has played an important role in those evolutions. In this paper the evolutions of the VIS optical design are summarized. The actual optical design covering 390-952nm simultaneously with a spectral resolution R > 4000 and for selected narrow wavebands with R > 18000 is presented in detail. The optimized instrument parameters have been taken fully into account to satisfy the multiplex requirement too. The dioptric cameras provide good image performance for both low and high resolution observing modes.

Items.Authors: David L. King, Nazim Ali Bharmal, David Bramall, Jenny King, Tim Morris, Jürgen Schmoll, Patrick Smith, Anjali Bhatt, Raziye Artan
Items.Title: MOSAIC at the ELT: the optical design of the ground layer adaptive optics (GLAO) natural guide star systems
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph and IFU instrument for the ESO ELT, currently in its design phase. The MOSAIC Ground Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) subsystem uses Laser Guide Star Systems (LGSS) and Natural Guide Star Systems (NGSS), each being Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensors (WFS). Light from the MOSAIC focal plane is passed to 4 GLAO boxes, each containing one LGSS and one NGSS. Common optics are shared between the LGSS and NGSS - a large focal reducing lens and dichroic to split the light between the two systems. The novel feature of the common optics are they reduce by a factor of 10 the focal planes of the laser guide star at the extreme distances and collimates the beam of the NGSS. A steering mirror at the NGSS pupil steers the field to the NGS WFS. The pupil is resized to match the ESO ALICE detector and the lenslet array is placed within the camera.  An additional metrology system in each GBOX also monitors relative motion between the GBOX and the MOSAIC focal plate.

Items.Authors: Yohko Tsuboi, Ryota Inoue, Rintaro Nishiyama, Ayaka Mitsubori, Takahiro Seguchi, Daiki Ishi, Yoshitomo Maeda, Tomokage Yoneyama, Wataru Buz Iwakiri
Items.Title: Multilayer crystal configuration of the Bragg-reflection x-ray spectropolarimeter ParaDAXAS for an extended energy range
Items.Abstract: Simultaneous X-ray spectroscopy and polarimetry are increasingly required to study high-energy astrophysical processes such as accretion flows near black holes and magnetic reconnection. However, conventional X-ray polarimeters cannot achieve both high energy resolution and a large modulation factor. We are developing ParaDAXAS, a Bragg-reflection optical system with curved crystals arranged on a paraboloidal surface of revolution, aiming to obtain high-resolution dispersed spectra in a defocused setup together with high-sensitivity polarimetry.  We demonstrate energy-band extension using multilayer (multi-d) crystal stacking. By stacking crystals with different lattice spacings, such as Si, Ge, and C, multiple energies satisfy the Bragg condition at the same incidence angle, widening the reflective bandwidth without degrading polarization selectivity. Using a Si(111)/Si(100) stack, we verified the intended Bragg planes and lower-layer Fe-K alpha reflection.

Items.Authors: Anand Nagesh
Items.Title: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS): a cloud-connected space and ground telescope network for real-time sky mapping and awareness
Items.Abstract: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS) is a new way of monitoring the sky—using a fleet of small telescopes in space, combined with ground observatories and cloud computing, to deliver real-time insights about what is happening above Earth. Instead of relying only on large, expensive observatories, NOaaS uses multiple compact telescopes in low-Earth orbit working together as a virtual global observatory. The NOaaS approach is built on five key pillars:  1. Space-Based Sky Coverage All Day, All Night  2. Global Hybrid Sensing (Space + Ground)  3. Real-Time Cloud Processing  4. Autonomous Operations  5.Open Access and Subscription Model

Items.Authors: Kazuhiro Nakazawa, Keigo Okuma, Shin'ichiro Takeda, Yuta Nishimura, Moeka Baba, Yuto Kobayashi, Yuki Omiya, Atsuya Tanaka, Shin Watanabe, Tadayuki Takahashi, Naoki Ishida, Mitstunobi Onishi, Toshihiko Arai, Hiroki Yoneda, Masamune Saito, Jun Kataoka
Items.Title: Narrow field of view Si/CdTe Compton telescope with high aspect-ratio coded mask; miniSGI - verification in the 511 keV to 1.8 MeV band
Items.Abstract: Semiconductor Compton telescope (SCT) is a promising device to improve the MeV sensitivity gap. Based on ASTRO-H/SGD, which adopted a deep well-type active shield to limit its field-of-view (FoV) to ~10 deg combined with a Si/CdTe Compton telescope to further reduce background in orbit, we are developing miniSGI, to demonstrate sub-degree angular resolution in the MeV band. Even for SCT, angular resolution in 0.5-1 MeV is about 2-4 deg, not enough to resolve celestial sources in Galactic center. miniSGI has one layer of 0.5 mm thick 250 µm pitch DSSD and another layer of 2 mm thick CdTe-DSD, which provides angular-resolution measure of <3 deg in 356 keV in Compton reconstruction. It is surrounded by 20 mm thick BGOs and combined with a 5 mm thick 0.8 mm pitch Tungsten coded mask. Using miniSGI, we achieved 0.25 deg Compton reconstruction coded-mask combined imaging of 511 keV. We are also verifying electron-track reconstruction of 1.27 and 1.8 MeV line gamma-rays with the system.

Items.Authors: G. Cobos Tello, D. Tcherniak, T. Wucher, T. Suleman, C. A. Oxborrow, I. Kuvvetli, D. Blánquez, A. Morello, D. D. M. Ferreira
Items.Title: NewAthena WFI: ECSS qualified onboard software production methodology for astronomical instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Currently, the main challenge for the qualification of onboard science software within the European space sector, is the stringent requirements imposed by the ECSS standard ECSS-E-ST-40C for critical software. This paper will present status on the implementation of an efficient solution that fulfils code verification requirements for the NewAthena WFI AIM.

Items.Authors: Romain Laugier, Jonah Hansen, Felix Dannert, Philipp Huber, Jens Kammerer, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Denis Defrère, Loes Rutten, Jeremy Scott
Items.Title: NIFITS: building a new data standard to enable the rise of nulling interferometry
Items.Abstract: So far, the nature of nulling interferometers has prevented the use of the OIFITS format used for classical beam-combiners. The new data format NIFITS, is on track for broad adoption not only by most nulling teams around the world (Asgard/NOTT, GLINT, LBTI, LIFE) but also by modelling tools such as OIModeller.  By including a high-fidelity parametric forward model of the instrument along with the data, it empowers the user to deploy the full extent of their reduction and modelling tools even when agnostic of the details of the instrument. To illustrate the power of NIFITS, we present some examples of results obtained during a hackathon held in August 2025.  This is leading to the consolidation of data reduction and interpretation algorithms shared horizontally between different projects and vertically from early concept evaluation phase to exploitation.

Items.Authors: S. Savorgnano, P. S. Barry, C. S. Benson, C. M. Bradford, T. L. R. Brien, S. Doyle, V. Gómez-Rivera, S. Hailey-Dunsheath, J. Hernández-Aguilar, J. L. Hernández Rebollar, D. H. Hughes, E. Kane, K. S. Karkare, A. Lapuente, R. McGeehan, R. Naranjo-Romero, A. Papageorgiou, J. G. Redford, I. Rodríguez-Montoya, S. Rowe, D. O. Sánchez-Argüelles, A. Tan, M. Becerril-Tapia, J. Vega-Mendez
Items.Title: Noise characterization of line intensity mapping observations with SuMAC at the LMT
Items.Abstract: The SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMAC) combines the SuperSpec on-chip spectrometer with the MUSCAT camera at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT) to explore future Line Intensity Mapping (LIM) observations. SuperSpec is a dual-polarization KID-based spectrometer covering the 190–320 GHz atmospheric window with a spectral resolution of R~120. We present a preliminary noise characterization of LIM-like observations acquired during the Summer 2025 campaign using scans of the galaxy cluster Abell 370. Power spectral density analyses of detector timestreams are used to investigate atmospheric and instrumental noise under different observing configurations, including varying scan speeds and observations with the optical chopper enabled and disabled. These results provide an initial assessment of instrument performance and establish a framework for future studies of atmospheric mitigation, detector correlations, and map-level sensitivity for upcoming SuperSpec LIM surveys.

Items.Authors: Maddalena Bugatti
Items.Title: Non-parametric PSF reconstruction and correction for accurate radial velocity measurements
Items.Abstract: Precise radial-velocity (RV) measurements at the m/s to cm/s level require an accurate knowledge of the spectrograph’s instrumental profile. Parametric PSF/LSF models often fail to capture asymmetries or chromatic variations, introducing systematic RV errors. I present a non-parametric method to reconstruct the LSF directly from laser frequency comb (LFC) calibration spectra. By modeling each comb mode with a flexible, data-driven representation, we recover the local LSF without assuming a functional form. The resulting LSF is used to deconvolve stellar spectra, removing instrumental broadening and revealing intrinsic line shapes. This approach improves profile fidelity, reduces RV biases from PSF variations, and offers a robust framework for tracking time-dependent instrumental behavior, enabling higher precision in exoplanet and stellar RV studies.

Items.Authors: Jim Tucker
Items.Title: Novel approach to deformable mirror (DM) actuation
Items.Abstract: A novel approach to deformable mirror (DM) actuation is presented that overcomes challenges common in current state-of-the-art approaches. DMs are typically actuated by voltage-driven means. The proposed DM utilizes discrete, radiantly heated, thermal expansion pistons as actuators. Multiple thermal expansion pistons sit between a thin mirror and a reaction structure, which also functions as a heatsink. There are "holes" below each piston, allowing radiant heat to be directed to the piston, inducing local thermal expansion. Heat is drained from the piston through physical connection to the reaction structure. The balance between heat input and dissipation rate controls the temperature of the piston, and thus its height. DM sensitivity, response, and recovery time can be tailored by material selection (CTE, specific heat, emissivity, and thermal conductivity) and geometry (thickness shape, and interface cross-section) to optimize performance for the desired application.

Items.Authors: Noboru Ebizuka, Takayuki Okamoto, Takuya Hosobata, Masahiro Takeda, Yutaka Yamagata, Minoru Sasaki, Makio Nishimaki, Kazuya Yamamoto, Yukinobu Nishio, Masahiro Konishi, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Kosuke Kushibiki, Hidenori Takahashi, Kentaro Motohara
Items.Title: Novel transmission gratings with large angular dispersion, high efficiency and wide spectral bandwidth II
Items.Abstract: We are developing several types of novel gratings, including a volume binary (VB) grating, trapezoid grating, reflector facet transmission (RFT) grating and prism array for a grism.　 The VB grating provides a larger angular dispersion and higher diffraction efficiency than a conventional surface-relief transmission grating with step shaped grooves, and broader spectral bandwidth than a volume phase holographic (VPH) grating. 　The trapezoid grating further improves the peak diffraction efficiency compared with the VB grating. 　The RFT grating is a novel transmission echelle grating which achieves both a higher diffraction efficiency and wider spectral bandwidth than conventional reflection echelle gratings. 　The prism-array enables us to reduce thickness of a grism along the optical axis and to increase its resolving power of the grism. 　The current status of development and initial performance of these gratings and prism arrays are presented.

Items.Authors: Ryan Swindle, Zach Gazak, Justin Fletcher
Items.Title: On-sky performance of a mobile, off-grid, robotic observatory for space domain awareness
Items.Abstract: Space domain awareness (SDA) is a rapidly growing niche in ground- and space-based astronomy, driven partly by 20--30% YOY growth in on-orbit population. Rising satellite density, launch rates, and conjunction risk demand a larger, faster-responding sensor network. In 2024, we presented the Deployable Attritable Optical (DAO) telescope as a concept. A collaboration between the U.S. Space Force (USSF) and commercial astronomy, this mobile, off-grid, robotic SDA observatory achieved first light in 2026 and now operates nightly. We review the design, now offered through Observable Space as a meter-class, f/2.25 folded prime focus Cassegrain telescope accommodating additional instrumentation. We then describe its modeled and measured detection performance for objects from LEO to xGEO, using USSF-developed open-source tools for observatory orchestration (SensorKit) and autonomous data processing (Burr) --- which welcome public participation --- presented separately in these proceedings.

Items.Authors: Joshua Oppor, Gary Hill, Hanshin Lee, Casey Kyte, Brian Vattiat, Niv Drory, John Good, Jason Vestuto, Gregory Zeimann
Items.Title: On-sky performance testing of the VIRUS2 fiber-fed integral field spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We evaluate VIRUS2 performance during the first phase of commissioning involving 1 of 6 identical units. A single unit contains 256 fibers each subtending 2.5” which are split into 4 spectral channels covering 370-930 nm at R>2000. With 1536 total fibers, the complete IFU covers a footprint of 1.7’ x 1.3’ on the McDonald Observatory 2.7 m Harlan J. Smith Telescope. Using 1/6 of the final footprint, we present the first end-to-end performance tests with full capability. We discuss some metrics of stability, fiber-to-fiber variations, and we evaluate the performance of the novel beam-switch module (BSM) by way of a ”bypass” test. Finally, we discuss the power and utility of VIRUS2 putting on display recent observations of the Ring Nebula where the combination of IFU footprint, spatial resolution, and spectral coverage are most effective.

Items.Authors: Federico Izraelevitch-Patitucci, Sarah Tolilla, Ilian Ellafi, Jean-Pierre Rivet, Mathilde Hugbart, Guillaume Labeyrie, Olivier Lai, Andreas Zmija, William Guerin, Robin Kaiser
Items.Title: On-sky single-photon time resolution of 35ps with White Rabbit synchronization: towards the measurement of the size of a white dwarf star
Items.Abstract: It is thought that more than 95 % of the stars in our Universe will end their life as a White Dwarf: the last stage of stellar evolution before thermal death. In these objects, the gravitational collapse is not supported by nuclear fusion, but by electron degeneracy, driven by the fermion’s statistics and the Pauli exclusion principle.    The IC4Stars (Intensity Correlation for Stars) project aims to measure the diameter of the white dwarf star Sirius B, using Intensity Interferometry. In this work we present our latest efforts and the milestones achieved in the last year. We report laboratory characterization of the single-photon detectors, TDC and synchronization electronics. We describe an observation campaign where we demonstrated on-sky time resolution below 35 ps RMS, synchronizing two TDCs using the White Rabbit protocol and a 30 m telecom fiber. We developed the data acquisition of the raw time tags, and an algorithm to compute the Second-order correlation function.

Items.Authors: Andrew Ferayorni, Sarah Jaeggli
Items.Title: Operational efficiency improvements for the DL-NIRSP instrument control system
Items.Abstract: The National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) is a 4-meter solar observatory in operation at Haleakalā, Hawaii. The Diffraction Limited Near Infrared Spectropolarimeter (DLNIRSP) is a key instrument at DKIST that measures magnetic fields and dynamics in the Sun's atmosphere. The DLNIRSP has a complex instrument control system with multiple camera and motion sub-systems that perform synchronized data acquisition sequences. Several improvements to the control system have been made recently to increase efficiency and reduce duty cycle. Optimizations in mechanism move times, field mapping patterns, and camera triggering schemes have yielded efficiency gains of up to 3X. In this paper we describe areas of the control system marked for improvement and different solutions considered. We review changes made to mechanism and camera timing and discuss how we verified our results. We conclude by discussing future optimizations that may improve efficiency further.

Items.Authors: Lixi Tang
Items.Title: Optical design of adaptive optics system for 600mm afocal telescope in long-baseline interferometric array
Items.Abstract: Long-baseline optical interferometry is achieved by combining multiple sub-telescopes into an equal large-aperture, high spatial resolution optical system. The wavefront quality of each sub-telescope will affect the contrast of the interference fringes. The optical design of the adaptive optics system for 600mm afocal telescopes presented. High speed deformable mirror and high sensitivity wavefront sensor are applied in our system to provide key devices for the adaptive optics system of the long-baseline interferometric telescope array under construction in China.

Items.Authors: Giorgio M. Pariani, Marco Bonaglia, Marco M. Riva, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: Optical design of the MORFEO low order WFS atmospheric dispersion corrector
Items.Abstract: MORFEO, the Multi-Conjugated Adaptive Optics (MCAO) module for the ELT, is equipped with three Low Order and Reference (LOR) modules, implementing the Natural Guide Star wavefront sensing functionalities. In this paper, after a description of the overall optical design of the LOR module, we concentrate on the ADC design, which is incredibly demanding, both in terms of dispersion and pointing accuracy. We will present the methodology we used for the glass selection, performed with a Matlab-based routine at the maximum Zenith angle. The best solutions were then optimized in Zemax at all Zenith angles, and ranked by dispersion residuals, sensitivity to thermal variations, prisms’ apex angles, pupil wobbling and glass availability and price. For the best candidate, we evaluated the sensitivity to the atmospheric model, manufacturing errors and temperature variations, to provide the expected performances in terms of dispersion and pointing of the LO WFS module.

Items.Authors: Morgane Loquet Le Gall, Creidhe O'Sullivan, Bruno Borgo, Clémence De Jabrun, Valentin Sauvage, N. Trappe, Bruno Maffei
Items.Title: Optical development of the BISOU breadboard
Items.Abstract: BISOU (Balloon Interferometer for Spectral Observations of the primordial Universe) is an astronomical balloon- borne pathfinder developed as part of a preparatory study for a future space mission aimed at measuring spectral distortions of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). A laboratory breadboard of the instrument is being developed at the Institut d’Astrophysique Spatiale (IAS), enabling the characterization of subsystems and in- strument systematic effects, particularly in the optical system. The optical system is based on a differential polarizing Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) that receives inputs from both a sky-facing telescope and an internal calibration source. The full spectral band, spanning between 90 and 1500 GHz. The optical analysis first relies on ray-tracing simulations to establish the overall configuration of the system, before proceeding to more advanced Gaussian beam and physical optics analyses.

Items.Authors: Carmelo Arcidiacono, Fernando Pedichini, Marco Riva, Gianluca Di Rico, Elisa Portaluri, Demetrio Magrin
Items.Title: Optical heterodyne long-baseline interferometry: a concept study of feasibility, photon budget, and science requirements
Items.Abstract: We explore the feasibility of Optical Heterodyne Long-Baseline Interferometry (OHLBI) for bright stellar and AGN science. Narrow-band heterodyne detection preserves phase beyond the atmospheric coherence time, enabling long integrations if photon-noise limits and Local Oscillator (LO) stability are controlled. Starting from the demonstrated performance of the Infrared Spatial Interferometer and earlier optical VLBI studies, we quantify expected SNR for key cases: surface imaging of bright O/B stars, time-resolved mapping of rapid rotators, eclipsing binaries, and kinematic studies of luminous AGN cores. We derive realistic photon budgets at visible and NIR wavelengths and identify regimes where heterodyne phase stability provides a scientific advantage over direct detection. We outline system requirements for a pathfinder, AO-fed receivers, comb-stabilized LOs and multi-site correlation, and define a roadmap toward future hybrid direct/heterodyne interferometry.

Items.Authors: M. Ito, T. Ogawa, H. Kondo, T. Matsuo, S. Ikari, R. Funase
Items.Title: Optical path difference control method for SEIRIOS mission and its applicability to future formation flying space-based interferometers
Items.Abstract: SEIRIOS is a formation flying micro-satellite mission for infrared interferometric observations using a densified pupil spectrograph. To obtain clear interference fringes, extremely strict optical path difference (OPD) control is required.  In this presentation, we propose a novel method that estimates the OPD from interference fringe images obtained by a densified pupil spectrograph and feeds it back to onboard actuators such as delay-line stages and tip–tilt mirrors. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through ground-based experiments and numerical simulations, showing that sub-micrometer-level OPD estimation and control can be achieved from a single image. Furthermore, by presenting the current OPD control sequence in the SEIRIOS mission, we demonstrate that the proposed method provides a highly promising approach for future OPD control in formation flying space-based interferometers.

Items.Authors: Qian Chen, Xufang Li
Items.Title: Optical performance of the AliCPT-1 Telescope
Items.Abstract: Ali CMB Polarization Telescope (AliCPT) is a 72 cm on-axis retracting telescope located at an altitude of 5250 m in Ali (Nagri) area of Tibet, China. It is the first project in the northern hemisphere designed for CMB polarization observation. The first state of AliCPT (AliCPT-1) has been deployed in April, 2025. AliCPT-1 has about 1700 transition edge sensor bolometers and supports observation capabilities at 90 GHz and 150 GHz. This presentation will report the performance of AliCPT-1. We present results from calibration campaign in situ at Ali, including detector spectral response, optical efficiency, near-field beam (NFBM), far-field beam (FFBM) and far-side lobe (FSLM).
